reports.title: Iris Fordham: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: The poor quality of recording clinical records impeded the Trust's governance processes, in that the author of a serious incident investigation was unable to rely on clear evidence to understand why essential actions were not carried out in Ms [name redacted] care.
The Trust failed to complete a falls risk assessment of Ms Fordham.
The consequence of (2) was that no falls care plan was completed.

The fact that the failures at (2) & (3) were not detected and remediated by successive clinical staff members suggests that they did not read essential parts of the clinical record when providing care. The cumulative failings, on the part of multiple healthcare professionals suggests a culture of indifference inimical to the provision of safe and effective practice.
The Trust has not considered any step to resolve individual failings in care through disciplinary or regulatory channels.
concerns.hazard: lack of disciplinary or regulatory action

promises.quote: A specific induction programme has been formulated for the A&E which specifically covers themes such as the mental capacity act, contemporaneous documentation including emergency administered drugs with rationale, sedation and also escalation.
promises.summary: Implement A&E induction covering MCA and contemporaneous documentation

promises.quote: The speciality medicine team have a teaching programme and induction of all levels of staff on Internal Professional standards and appropriate contemporaneous documentation.
promises.summary: Teach staff on professional standards and documentation

promises.quote: Teams will ensure that consultants on call confirm that they have remote access to the electronic healthcare record, this will eliminate the risk that documentation is not completed in relation to critical decisions.
promises.summary: Ensure consultants confirm remote EHR access

promises.quote: The Trust are supportive of staff that are increasingly managing high numbers of complex and acutely unwell patients. In this case, doctors sought and were provided with advice from a consultant on call. The consultant on call will attend to perform certain procedures (in line with the Royal College of Emergency Medicine guidance).
promises.summary: Consultant on call to attend for high-acuity cases

promises.quote: The speciality medicine team have a teaching programme and induction of all levels of staff on Internal Professional standards and appropriate contemporaneous documentation.

promises.quote: WXH have very carefully considered PFDs issued by the coroner in conjunction with late submissions and the impact this has on families, HM Coroner and ensuring preparedness for inquests. Steps have been taken to ensure that specialities have early sight of inquests.
promises.summary: Ensure specialties have early sight of inquests

concerns.quote: Documentation of key stages in Mr [name redacted] care was poor or non-existent. Critical decisions on; mental capacity, best interests, the choice of sedation, the amount of drug administered, the method of administration and the timing of administration were not clearly recorded.
The decision to sedate Mr Morton was flawed. The lack of contemporary documentation impeded an effective coronial investigation and review of that clinical decision.

A failure in governance at the Trust meant that this case was not identified as a serious incident. This omission gives rise to a concern that future deaths may follow due to an inability on the part of the trust to identify, reflect upon, and remediate sub-optimal practice
the trust's Datix incident reporting system, morbidity and mortality meeting process and SIRMAP procedure were inadequate. Each structure was siloed from the other, leading to inconsistent findings.
concerns.hazard: inadequate incident reporting and review systems

reports.title: Mohammad Asghar: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: A failure in governance at the Trust meant that this case was not identified as an incident worthy of investigation through the Patient Safety Framework. This omission gives rise to a concern that future deaths may follow due to an inability on the part of the trust to identify, reflect upon, and remediate sub-optimal practice. In this case the trust's Datix incident reporting system, morbidity and mortality meeting process and PSIRF procedure were inadequate.

Despite concerns being raised by a medical examiner, a coroner's court finding that an iatrogenic injury was contributory to death, and an express direction from this court for the case to be reviewed, no patient safety framework investigation has occurred.

Correspondence received from the Trust sent three months after the inquest that seeks to explain why a PSRF investigation was not undertaken in this case betrays the fact that senior governance staff at the Trust still do not understand NHS England guidance on what should trigger a patient safety investigation.
